title: God, the Offended God Most High
description: God, the Offended God Most High in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 11.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God, the of-fend-ed God most high, Am-bas-sa-dors to re-bels sends; His mess-en-gers his place sup-ply, And Je-sus begs us to be friends.

lines: God, the offended God most high,
And Jesus begs us to be friends.
Us, in the stead of Christ, they pray,
Us, in the stead of God, intreat,
To cast our arms, our sins, away,
And find forgiveness at his feet.
Our God in Christ! thine embassy,
Poor debtors, by our Lord's request
We, at our Judge's instance, live!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
